Title: PM has no power to direct project awards, High Court told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The prime minister has no authority under the law and government procurement regulations to direct that a project be awarded to a particular company, the High Court heard today.
Former Finance Ministry procurement division secretary Datuk Zamzuri Abdul Aziz said the authority to determine whether a project should be implemented through pre-qualification or direct negotiation rested with the Finance Minister.
He was testifying in the trial of former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, who faces charges of using his position and money laundering in connection with the Jana Wibawa programme.
Deputy public prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin asked Zamzuri whether the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) was involved in the procurement and assessment process for KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd.
"Yes," he replied.
KCJ Engineering, an engineering and construction company alleged to have contributed RM800,000 to Bersatu, was awarded a road construction project linking Felda Bukit Jalor and Gemas, Negri Sembilan, under Jana Wibawa through direct negotiation.
Zamzuri agreed that KCJ Engineering had initially failed the preliminary assessment by the Jana Wibawa Contractor Evaluation Committee.
Wan Shaharuddin: Usually, if a company fails the assessment, it will not be approved or considered, correct?
Zamzuri: Yes.
Wan Shaharuddin: Following that, did the PMO submit additional information through a letter dated Nov 13, 2020?
Zamzuri: Yes.
Wan Shaharuddin: Who would know why the information was provided?
Zamzuri: I am not sure.
Yesterday, Finance Ministry procurement division secretary Rosni Mohd Yusoff told the court that KCJ Engineering had failed its initial assessment when she chaired the Contractor Evaluation Committee meeting.
Rosni, who was then MoF Government Investment Companies Division secretary, said the assessment followed a proposal by Muhyiddin to appoint the company.
She said the ministry subsequently received a letter from the PMO requesting a reassessment.
The committee, which met on Feb 26, 2021, subsequently found that KCJ Engineering had met all the required criteria.
Earlier, Zamzuri said he had instructed Rosni, then his deputy and chairman of the Contractor Evaluation Committee, to assess KCJ Engineering after the company was listed in a PMO letter dated Nov 13, 2020.
"The letter was sent to the then finance minister, Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Tengku Abdul Aziz. It was then minuted to me for action, namely to conduct an assessment of the company.
"If the name KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd had not been stated in the prime minister's letter dated Nov 13, 2020, the Contractor Evaluation Committee would not have assessed the company.
"This was because assessments were only conducted on companies proposed by the PMO," he said in his witness statement.
Zamzuri said KCJ Engineering would not have been awarded the project by the Public Works Department (PWD) without first undergoing the MoF committee's assessment.
He said every contractor appointment under Jana Wibawa through direct negotiation had to undergo the committee's assessment before price negotiations and the issuance of a Letter of Acceptance by PWD.
The trial before Judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin continues tomorrow.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: DAP's equal allocations call not discussed at Cabinet meeting - Fahmi
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: DAP's call for equal constituency development allocations for all members of parliament was not discussed at today's Cabinet meeting, government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said.
The communications minister said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was aware of the matter adding that it may be discussed by the Cabinet at a later date.
"It was not discussed at today's cabinet meeting. But the Prime Minister is certainly aware of the matter. It may be discussed in the future," he said at his weekly post-Cabinet media briefing here today.
This follows a call by DAP national chairman Gobind Singh Deo for Anwar to honour Pakatan Harapan's election pledge to provide equal constituency development allocations to all MPs.
Gobind also urged the government to enact a legislation to institutionalise equal allocations and remove political discretion from the distribution of constituency development funds.
He said PH's election manifesto had expressly committed to providing equal development allocations to all MPs, based on the principle that voters should not be disadvantaged because of their political choices or affiliations.
Gobind acknowledged Anwar's recent announcement of additional direct funds for each parliamentary constituency, but said this did not resolve the broader issue of equal and non-discriminatory allocations.
He urged the government to first provide equal allocations to all MPs before enacting legislation to permanently guarantee the arrangement.
The issue has also drawn attention following reports that several MPs had lost access to the MyKhas portal, which is used to administer federal constituency development allocations.
On May 22,
then-Subang MP Wong Chen
said his office had been denied access to the portal without prior notice. Petaling Jaya MP Lee Chean Chung and Ampang MP Rodziah Ismail also reported similar restrictions.
The three MPs were among PKR lawmakers who attended a press conference by former party leaders Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli and Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad announcing the formation of Bersama.
On Aug 7, Anwar defended the government's position, saying allocations for parliamentary constituencies were intended for constituents and were not the exclusive right of the elected MP.
Meanwhile,
Gobind has also called on Anwar
to ensure key institutional reforms are implemented by the end of the year.
These include separating the roles of the Attorney General and Public Prosecutor, limiting the Prime Minister's tenure to two terms, and amending the Security Offences (Special Measures) Act (Sosma) and the Peaceful Assembly Act.
Gobind said the groundwork for the separation of the Attorney General and Public Prosecutor's roles, as well as the proposed two-term limit for prime ministers, had already been completed.
He said amendments to Sosma and the Peaceful Assembly Act should also be finalised and tabled without further delay.

Title: Motorcycle noise complaint sparks fight, 3 injured in Penampang
Article:
PENAMPANG: A complaint about a motorcycle's loud engine noise escalated into a fight that left three men injured at Kampung Muhibbah, Petagas, here last night.
The incident, which occurred about 9.30pm, is believed to have started after one of the victims confronted the suspect, who was also his neighbour, as he rode his motorcycle through the area.
Penampang district police chief Superintendent Sammy Newton said police received information about a fight involving a group of people who were gathered and playing carrom outside a house.
He said initial investigations found that the 37-year-old suspect had ridden through the area on a motorcycle, producing a loud engine noise.
"One of the victims then confronted the suspect before an argument broke out and escalated into a fight.
"Three men aged between 35 and 40 were injured after a sharp object was used during the incident," he said in a statement today.
Sammy said all three victims were treated at Queen Elizabeth Hospital in Kota Kinabalu and were reported to be in stable condition.
He said following the incident, a team from the Penampang district police headquarters Criminal Investigation Division and Putatan police station arrested the suspect at a village in Putatan at about 10pm.
"Initial investigations found that the incident was believed to have occurred spontaneously following a misunderstanding and the suspect's dissatisfaction after being confronted over the motorcycle noise.
"So far, there is no record of any previous dispute or grudge between the suspect and the victims," he said.
Sammy said investigations were ongoing, including recording statements from several witnesses and examining closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage at the scene to complete the investigation papers.
"The case is being investigated under Section 326 of the Penal Code, and the investigation papers will be referred to the prosecution for further action.
"Police also advise the public not to spread unverified information or upload images and videos of the incident, which could hamper investigations and cause public concern," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar hails Bukit Mertajam Hospital's global green recognition
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated Bukit Mertajam Hospital on its global recognition as a Green Hospital.
The hospital is the only one in Malaysia to be listed among the world's top 250 hospitals for sustainability initiatives.
Anwar described the achievement as a source of pride for the country, highlighting the importance of combining excellence in healthcare with environmental responsibility and public wellbeing.
"This is an achievement that makes the country proud, where excellence in healthcare services goes hand in hand with the responsibility to preserve the environment and ensure the wellbeing of the people," he said in a social media post.
Bukit Mertajam Hospital has been recognised among the world's top 250 greenest hospitals in Newsweek and Statista's World's Greenest Hospitals 2026 ranking, making it the only Malaysian hospital to receive this international recognition for climate action and environmental sustainability.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: FB, TikTok account for 92pct of scam content flagged for removal
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Some 127,568 scam-related online content items have been flagged for removal as of today, with Facebook and TikTok accounting for 53 per cent and 39 per cent respectively.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the content included false claims, such as unannounced additional Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) payments purportedly from the Finance Ministry.
He said the figure represented 27 per cent of the total requests for content removal.
"Of these, 53 per cent was on Facebook, 39 per cent on TikTok, while the remainder was on other platforms," he said at a post-cabinet meeting press conference today.
Fahmi, who is also Communications Minister, said fake accounts remained a major problem, particularly in scam activities, as they could be easily created and used to spread false information rapidly.
"We see that Facebook and TikTok are the two platforms where the highest number of scam-related crimes have been detected. But this is based only on what has been reported," he said.
He said the government had provided platforms such as Sebenarnya.my and MyCheck to enable the public to verify information, and encouraged them to seek confirmation through mainstream media.
In a related development, Fahmi said the government had issued and gazetted two codes -- the Child Protection Code (CPC) and Risk Mitigation Code (RMC) -- that social media platforms are required to comply with.
He said the platforms had been given several months to implement coordinated measures to prevent harmful content that could threaten property or lives.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Solarvest Q1 earnings up 19.8pct on stronger revenue, associate contributions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Solarvest Holdings Bhd's net profit rose 19.8 per cent to RM19.02 million in the first quarter ended June 30, 2026, from RM15.87 million a year earlier, driven by higher revenue and increased contributions from associates and joint ventures.
Revenue grew 13.2 per cent to RM155.93 million from RM137.74 million, mainly supported by utility-scale projects, including multiple Large Scale Solar 5 (LSS5) developments and ongoing works under the Corporate Green Power Programme.
In a bourse filing, Solarvest said the renewable energy (RE) industry continued to have positive prospects, underpinned by the government's target to increase RE's share of the national energy mix to 70 per cent and achieve net-zero emissions by 2050.
As at end-June, Malaysia had reached nearly 33 per cent installed RE capacity, reflecting continued progress in clean energy infrastructure and the country's energy transition.
"Looking ahead, solar energy is expected to remain the primary driver of RE growth, supported by continued policy initiatives and capacity expansion, with the power sector targeted to achieve 40 per cent RE capacity by 2035," it said.
Solarvest said it remains focused on growing its order book by tapping opportunities under LSS6, the Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme and the Solar Accelerated Transition Action Programme.
Its unbilled order book stood at RM2.37 billion as at June 30, 2026, which will be recognised in the financial years ending March 31, 2027 and 2028.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Immigration lorry crash: Two drivers remanded for probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have remanded two drivers involved in a fatal collision involving an Immigration Department lorry that killed a father and his two daughters along Jalan Sultan Ismail early today.
Kuala Lumpur Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the drivers of the Proton Saga and the lorry were remanded for a day to facilitate investigations.
"We have remanded the driver of the Proton Saga and the driver of the lorry for a day," he said when contacted.

Title: Miros: Road safety not just public safety issue, but economic priority
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Reducing road fatalities is not merely a public safety agenda but a strategic investment to safeguard national productivity and economic growth, says the Malaysian Institute of Road Safety Research (Miros).
In a statement, Miros clarified that the estimated RM30 billion in socioeconomic losses from road crashes last year was calculated using the Value of Statistical Life (VOSL) methodology, based on fatality and serious injury data recorded by the police.
It said 6,537 deaths were recorded in 2025, with about 66 per cent involving motorcyclists, making them the highest-risk group of road users.
"The estimated RM30 billion in losses was nearly three times the total motor insurance premiums paid in the same year.
"The figure also amounted to a significant portion of the government's operating expenditure for 2025, highlighting the substantial economic burden on the country," it said.
Miros said the VOSL approach took into account loss of productivity and income, medical treatment costs, as well as pain, suffering and long-term psychological effects on families.
"VOSL does not represent the 'price' of a person's life, but rather an estimate of the economic value of reducing the risk of death.
"The findings underscore that efforts to reduce road crashes are not merely a road safety agenda, but a strategic investment to safeguard productivity, public wellbeing and the country's economic growth," it said.
On Monday, Miros presented its findings on the socioeconomic impact of road crashes in Malaysia at the Cabinet Committee Meeting on Road Safety and Congestion No. 1/2026, chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
Following the presentation,
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi
said Malaysia incurred up to RM30 billion in socioeconomic losses annually due to road crashes.
He said the figure was based on the economic value associated with fatalities, including lost productivity and income, treatment costs, and the impact on families and society.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Only 352 Malaysians have applied for 3D jobs so far on MyFutureJobs portal
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Despite thousands of positions offered in the 'dirty, dangerous and difficult' (3D) jobs sector, only 352 applications have come from Malaysians so far on the MyFutureJobs website.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said that while priority for the jobs is given to Malaysians, the numbers showed a gap between available jobs and the take-up rate by Malaysians.
"When the jobs are offered on MyFutureJobs, and no Malaysians come forward to take them, only then would we open them up to foreign workers, refugees or others," he said.
Ramanan was speaking to reporters at the ministry's monthly assembly and its Merdeka month celebration at Menara Perkeso here today.
Also present was his deputy, Datuk Khairul Firdaus Akbar Khan.
Ramanan was commenting on a suggestion by the Malaysian Humanitarian Organisation (MHO), which wanted the government to postpone the hiring of 15,000 foreign workers for the 3D sector and instead offer them to the stateless community in Malaysia.
On Monday, MHO submitted a memorandum of protest to the Prime Minister's Office regarding the government's directive to expedite the processing of 15,000 applications for foreign workers to meet labour needs for certain sectors.
MHO secretary-general Datuk Hishammuddin Hashim said the stateless community should be given the opportunity to work in Malaysia as they have resided here for a long time, with some even comprising fourth- or fifth-generation refugees.
This approach, he said, would not only meet labour needs but also possibly change the status of the stateless from a liability to an asset for the country.
Meanwhile, Ramanan said that while the manpower needs of the 3D sector number in the tens of thousands, applications from Malaysians remain low.
He said the government would continue to ensure that labour policies are beneficial to the people and country.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Selangor govt refers religious school sexual assault case to police
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The Selangor government has referred a sexual assault case involving a teacher at a religious school in the state to police for investigation.
State Islamic Affairs executive councillor Dr Mohammad Fahmi Ngah said the state government viewed the matter seriously and expressed regret over the incident.
He said teachers at religious schools were expected to serve not only as educators but also as guardians of students in their physical, mental and emotional development.
"We hope the police will conduct a thorough investigation and ensure the suspect faces appropriate action," he said.
Fahmi said he was confident the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (JAIS) would take appropriate action under existing laws, including reviewing the school's registration if necessary.
He said JAIS had taken measures to prevent misconduct involving teachers and students, teachers among themselves, and students.
JAIS also remains open to complaints from students or any party about suspected harassment or sexual assault at schools and hostels, he said.
Fahmi stressed that legal action would be taken immediately against offenders without compromise, adding that schools must remain safe environments for children.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ramkarpal urges Sanusi to respect Federal Court ruling on Kedah gambling ban
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: DAP lawmaker Ramkarpal Singh has urged Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor to respect the Federal Court ruling on the state's gambling premises ban.
The Bukit Gelugor member of parliament's call came after Sanusi said the state government respected the Federal Court's decision to dismiss Kedah's application for leave to appeal against a ruling declaring its ban on gambling premises unlawful.
Sanusi, speaking in Kuala Ketil, said the
state government was seeking further clarification
from its legal team on the full implications of the court's ruling.
Ramkarpal, however, said Sanusi should not seek ways to circumvent the decision, which could potentially amount to contempt of court.
"Sanusi should accept the fact that licensed gambling has been a part of Malaysian life and licences for the operation of gambling-related businesses are permitted under the Federal Constitution," he said in a statement today.
Ramkarpal, who is also DAP National Legal Bureau chairman, said Sanusi should focus on more effective enforcement measures to address Muslims participating in gambling activities.
He urged the Kedah government to engage federal agencies, including the Finance Ministry, police, Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and local authorities.
He said such cooperation would be more effective in tackling illegal gambling while respecting the legal status of licensed gambling operations.
Ramkarpal also warned that attempts to curb licensed gambling could result in increased illegal gambling activities, including those conducted online by individuals or syndicates.
He said the Federal Court's latest decision had settled the issue of licensed gambling and Sanusi should accept that such activities were legal.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thai worker charged with sexually assaulting teenage cousin
Article:
KOTA BARU: A Thai plantation worker was charged in the Sessions Court here today with three counts of sexually assaulting his 17-year-old female cousin in May and June.
The 25-year-old pleaded not guilty to all three charges before Judge Zulkifli Abdullah.
According to the first charge, the accused allegedly committed the offence against the victim, aged 17 years and seven months, with sexual intent at a bedroom in an unnumbered house in Kampung Lepan Anjung, Dabong, Kuala Krai, between 2am and 3am on May 31.
He was accused of committing a similar offence against the victim at the same location and time on June 1 under the second charge.
For the third charge, he was accused of committing the same offence at the same location between 2am and 3am on June 13.
All three charges were framed under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, which carries a maximum 20-year jail term and whipping upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Syazalia Che Suhaimin prosecuted, while the accused was unrepresented.
During the proceedings, Syazalia did not propose bail, saying the offences were non-bailable and the accused was a foreigner.
The accused was denied bail.
The court set Sept 20 for mention to allow the accused to appoint a lawyer.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police probe Shah Alam school bullying, 17-year-old suspect out on bail
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Police have opened an investigation into a bullying incident involving a 15-year-old student at a secondary school here, with the 17-year-old suspect released on bail after being remanded.
Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the case was being investigated under Sections 506 and 323 of the Penal Code for criminal intimidation and voluntarily causing hurt.
"The investigation is ongoing, and statements and information have been recorded.
"The 17-year-old suspect, who is a schoolmate of the victim, was arrested and remanded before being released on bail.
"Based on the statements obtained so far, the incident stemmed from teasing between schoolmates," he said at a press conference at the Selangor police headquarters here today.
Shazeli said police could not comment on the severity of the victim's injuries as they were still awaiting an official medical report.
He said only one suspect had been arrested so far, with the investigation to be completed before the investigation papers are referred to the deputy public prosecutor's office.
It was previously reported that the 15-year-old victim was at risk of hearing loss after allegedly being bullied and assaulted at a secondary school in Shah Alam.
The victim's mother, Nurhaswaty Zamani, 43, said her son, Adryz Adrian, suffered head and ear injuries following the alleged incident.
She said she only learned about the incident after her son returned from school last Wednesday and told her what had happened.
Nurhaswaty also claimed that her son had faced harassment from the same group of students since Form One.
"Only after this incident occurred and the school came under pressure from its superiors were the previous incidents also disclosed to me," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cabinet did not discuss Anwar's Taiwan remarks, says Fahmi
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The cabinet did not discuss Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's remarks on Taiwan, which drew a strong rebuke from Taipei, says government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
The Communications Minister said the issue was not raised during the cabinet meeting.
"It was not discussed," he said at a press conference after the cabinet meeting here today.
Fahmi was asked about a statement issued by Taiwan's Foreign Ministry yesterday criticising Anwar's remarks during a recent interview with Al Jazeera.
In the interview, Anwar expressed support for the One China policy and said historical factors should be considered when examining Taiwan's relationship with China.
He also said Taiwan was part of China and that the issue should ultimately be left to the Chinese people.
The remarks prompted a strong response from Taiwan's Foreign Ministry, which accused Anwar of making "false" statements and suggesting that Taiwan was a breakaway province of China while openly rationalising Beijing's position on the use of force to reunify Taiwan.
The ministry reaffirmed that Taiwan was a sovereign and independent country and was not subordinate to the People's Republic of China.
It said that status would not be changed by claims made by others.
Taipei also warned that Anwar's remarks could undermine regional peace and stability and affect the confidence of Taiwanese businesses investing in Malaysia.
"Considering that Malaysia is a democracy and Anwar has long portrayed himself as a defender of democracy and human rights, he should value principles such as freedom, human rights and the rule of law, and respect and uphold the will of the people," the ministry said.
It added that Anwar's comments effectively legitimised Beijing's position on the use of force against Taiwan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Cabinet approves National Border Plan for immediate action
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The cabinet has approved the Comprehensive National Border Plan for immediate implementation, says government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
The Communications Minister said the plan was presented by the Home Ministry and Transport Ministry at today's cabinet meeting.
"There are several matters that were presented by both the Home Ministry and Transport Ministry. As some of them involve security aspects, I would refer you to the Home Ministry for specific information.
"But the plan has been presented and approved by the cabinet for immediate action, starting today," he said at his weekly post-cabinet media briefing.
Fahmi did not elaborate on the specific security measures under the plan, referring questions on the matter to the Home Ministry.
The plan comes amid efforts to strengthen security and enforcement at the country's entry points, including airports, land borders and other gateways.
Earlier, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said a
comprehensive plan to improve controls
at the country's entry points would be tabled at the cabinet meeting.
He said the plan would be jointly presented with Transport Minister Anthony Loke, as it involved matters under the Transport Ministry's jurisdiction.
The plan was prepared within two weeks following a cabinet directive to strengthen controls at the country's entry points through greater coordination among relevant agencies.
Earlier this month, the cabinet instructed the Home and Transport ministries to submit a comprehensive plan to improve security controls at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) within two weeks.
The directive followed concerns over several recent incidents that could affect the country's image, as well as perceptions of weaknesses in the airport's security control system.
Airport security controls came under scrutiny following several cases involving Malaysians, including the detention of a Malaysian pilot after about 25kg of MDMA was seized at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Indonesia recently.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fire disaster declared in Sandakan after 28 houses destroyed
Article:
SANDAKAN: The Sandakan District Disaster Management Committee today declared a fire disaster in the district after a blaze destroyed 28 houses at Pulau Nunuyan Laut early this morning.
Its chairman Datuk Walter Kenson said the declaration was made at 9am based on reports and information received from agencies on the ground.
In a statement, he said a temporary relief centre (PPS) was opened at Masjid Al Fattah, Kampung Nunuyan Laut, at 10am following the declaration.
He said the centre was activated after the affected homes were deemed unsafe for occupation, with victim registration now underway.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt urged to clarify legal status of liquid nicotine after appeal withdrawal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government must clarify the legal status of liquid and gel nicotine used in vape products following its withdrawal of an appeal against a High Court ruling that invalidated the exemption of nicotine from the poisons list.
Malaysian Council for Tobacco Control (MCTC) secretary-general Muhammad Sha'ani Abdullah said the government should also clarify the relationship between the Poisons Act and the Control of Smoking Products for Public Health Act 2024 (Act 852) to avoid conflict in the legal framework governing nicotine and vaping.
He said Act 852 did not, by itself, legalise liquid nicotine, although it regulated smoking and vaping products, including prohibiting their sale to those below 18.
"The government must review the compatibility of Act 852 with the Poisons Act, including all subsidiary regulations relating to vaping.
"It should also determine whether liquid nicotine remained subject to controls under the Poisons Act or whether it intended to introduce a new exemption through a legally valid process.
"Clear enforcement guidance should also be provided pending final clarification of the legal position," he said in a statement today.
He said this when asked to comment on the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) withdrawal of the government's appeal against the High Court ruling that the removal of liquid nicotine used in vape and e-cigarette products from the poisons list was irrational and made without proper consultation with the Poisons Board.
Sha'ani said the withdrawal of the appeal went beyond ending the court dispute, as it created a need for the government to reconcile Malaysia's legal framework governing nicotine and vaping.
He said there was no scientific basis for allowing the inhalation of foreign substances into the lungs other than clean air.
"Smoking tobacco products as a long-practised habit can never be a justification for human-invented devices to be legally condoned for smoking," he said.
The judicial review was brought by the MCTC, Malaysian Green Lung Association and Voice of the Children.
The groups had challenged the government's decision to exempt nicotine liquids and gels used in e-cigarettes and vape products from poisons control.
The exemption was introduced through the Poisons (Amendment of Poisons List) Order 2023, which was gazetted on April 1, 2023.
The High Court ruled in May that the decision to remove liquid nicotine from the Poisons List was irrational and made without proper consultation with the Poisons Board.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Khaled: Regional uncertainty, emerging threats underpin higher defence spending
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's push for higher defence spending is driven not only by regional security developments but also by emerging threats including cyberattacks, electromagnetic threats and mass misinformation.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said these evolving challenges required Malaysia to enhance its defence assets and capabilities.
"All this demands a more adequate preparation and enhancement in our defence assets and capabilities.
"Nevertheless, in the context of the regional security landscape, I think this has to be looked at in the broader context of growing geopolitical uncertainty and the changing security environment in our region," he said in a statement.
Khaled was speaking following
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's call
for higher defence spending and stronger defence capabilities in Sabah, amid concerns over US military expansion in the Philippines.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, yesterday said the need for stronger defence capabilities must be viewed against shifting regional geopolitics, particularly rising tensions between the United States and China.
Khaled said the push did not mean Malaysia viewed any particular country as a threat but the potential unintended consequences of increased military activity and presence in the region.
"We do not. But there is clearly an increase in military activity and presence in the region, particularly as strategic competition between the major powers intensifies.
"When one side increases its presence or capabilities, it is natural that others may respond accordingly. This creates a more complex security environment for countries like Malaysia," he said.
He explained that when there are more military assets operating within a relatively confined geographical space, the possibility of miscalculation, misunderstanding or even a small incident escalating into something more serious naturally increases.
"Geographic proximity is therefore an important consideration for us. Developments around the southern Philippines, including areas close to Sabah, are geographically very near Malaysia.
"Even if an incident does not directly involve Malaysia, any escalation in areas close to us could have wider implications for our security and for stability in the South China Sea," he said.
At the same time, Khaled said Malaysia respected the Philippines' right, like any sovereign country, to determine its own defence arrangements and partnerships based on its security requirements.
"Malaysia maintains good relations with the Philippines, and it is important that we continue to have open lines of communication to manage any potential misunderstanding.
"Those are bilateral decisions for the countries concerned. Malaysia maintains good relations with the Philippines, and it is important that we continue to have open lines of communication to manage any potential misunderstanding," he said
Khaled said Malaysia's defence posture should not be viewed as the country choosing sides amid strategic competition between major powers.
He said efforts to strengthen defence preparedness were aimed at protecting Malaysia's sovereignty and national interests, rather than targeting the Philippines, the United States, China or any other country.
"The modernisation of the armed forces has already been part of our long-term national defence planning. The intention to gradually increase defence spending towards 1.5 per cent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) by 2030 should also be understood in that context.
"We are also strengthening capabilities in areas that are strategically important to Malaysia, including Pulau Layang-Layang. Again, this is about national defence and national interest, rather than responding to or targeting any particular country," he said.
He said Malaysia's approach would continue along two tracks — maintaining sufficient capabilities to protect its sovereignty and national interests while pursuing stability, dialogue and diplomacy.
"For the South China Sea, we hope all parties continue to exercise restraint and avoid actions that could lead to escalation.
"Progress on the Code of Conduct is also important in providing a more predictable environment for everyone.
"Malaysia will continue to support Asean Centrality and the Asean approach of providing space for dialogue, even where there are differences and overlapping claims. We want the region to remain stable, open and peaceful. That remains our priority," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Cabinet orders study on proposed hybrid GST-SST system
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The cabinet has directed the Finance Ministry to conduct a comprehensive study into a proposed hybrid Goods and Services Tax (GST)-Sales and Services Tax (SST) system.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan had been given time to prepare a report before bringing the matter back to the cabinet for further discussion.
"This is still at an early stage, and the Finance Ministry has been given time because this is not something that can be done hastily.
"It involves lessons from the implementation of the GST and issues faced under the current SST system, which will be considered by the Finance Ministry before the matter is brought back for discussion and a decision by the cabinet," he said at his weekly post-cabinet media briefing today.
Fahmi, who is also Communications Minister, said no timeline had been set for the study, including whether it would be ready for the upcoming Budget.
The study follows recent remarks by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim that the government was open to examining ways
to combine elements of the two tax systems
to develop a more progressive and efficient tax regime.
Anwar said, however, that the existing SST framework remained the basis of the country's tax system and that he did not support a broad-based tax that would burden those who currently did not pay tax.
GST, a multi-stage consumption tax, was introduced in April 2015 at 6 per cent but was abolished and zero-rated on June 1, 2018.
It was replaced by SST on Sept 1, 2018, in line with the manifesto of the then Pakatan Harapan-led administration.
Experts told the New Straits Times that a
GST-SST hybrid could strengthen revenue collection
while addressing weaknesses in the current system.
KPMG Malaysia head of tax Soh Lian Seng said one of the most useful GST features that could be adapted into SST was the input tax credit (ITC) mechanism, particularly for business-to-business transactions.
"Under the present SST regime, businesses often bear embedded taxes that cannot be recovered, resulting in tax cascading.
"A limited and targeted credit mechanism for certain sectors or transactions could help reduce these inefficiencies without necessarily moving to a full GST model."
Bank Muamalat Malaysia chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid cautioned that implementation should not become burdensome for Malaysians, citing the impact of delayed ITC refunds on businesses.
Meanwhile, SME Association of Malaysia national president Chin Chee Seong said the association supported the government considering GST, but stressed that any changes should not create another layer of compliance costs for businesses.
The government has repeatedly dismissed calls to reinstate GST.
Anwar said in June last year that it would only be considered when Malaysia's minimum wage exceeded RM4,000.
In December last year, Barisan Nasional chairman and Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the coalition would push for GST to be reinstated after the 16th General Election, describing it as the best tax regime to ensure fairness and stronger national revenue.
Zahid, who is also deputy prime minister, said BN's position was clear, although it was prepared to allow the existing SST system to continue for the time being.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Anwar orders review of TalentCorp's handling of doctors' return applications
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has instructed the Human Resources Ministry to review TalentCorp's handling of applications, including those from doctors seeking to return to Malaysia to serve.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Anwar had directed the ministry to report to the cabinet on applications received, processing times, approvals and rejections.
He said the review followed several matters raised with Anwar by the Malaysian Medical Council (MMC).
"The prime minister has asked the Human Resources Ministry to examine and report back to the cabinet on one of the agencies under the ministry, TalentCorp, particularly regarding the status of applications received, the processing period, how many have been approved and how many rejected, including applications involving doctors who want to return to Malaysia to serve," he said at his weekly post-cabinet media briefing today.
Fahmi said the review was aimed at giving the cabinet a clearer picture of TalentCorp's handling of applications and the issues raised by the MMC.
TalentCorp is responsible for initiatives to attract and retain skilled Malaysian talent, including facilitating the return of Malaysians working overseas.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rocky's death: Public advised against holding rallies, demonstrations ahead of charges tomorrow
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar today advised the public against holding rallies or demonstrations over the death of a dog during an enforcement operation in Port Klang last month.
He said police had completed their investigation and identified those responsible, with charges expected to be brought at the Klang magistrate's court tomorrow.
"I advise against escalating this issue to the point of holding any rally or demonstration because, from a legal standpoint, the investigation has been completed and we have identified the parties responsible.
"The outcome of our investigation has led to instructions for charges to be brought tomorrow. This shows that we have not taken sides.
"As long as there is a violation of the law, we will investigate and take action in accordance with the law," he said at a press conference at the Selangor police Headquarters here today.
Shazeli said the charges followed instructions from the deputy public prosecutor's office after the investigation was completed.
"God willing, the charges are expected to be brought at the Klang magistrate's court tomorrow. I urge members of the media to refer to the court for the exact time of the proceedings."
He declined to elaborate on whether the charges would involve the man and woman previously linked to the case or the specific legal provisions to be used.
Shazeli urged the public to give the legal process space and trust the authorities to carry out their responsibilities.
On security at the Klang court tomorrow, he said police would maintain security and public order throughout the proceedings.
He urged those attending to comply with police instructions and avoid causing any disturbance.
"Let the law do its work," he said.
Police had previously said the case was being investigated under Section 428 of the Penal Code for causing the death of an animal with intent to cause wrongful loss or damage.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia must strengthen maritime logistics as Asean trade surges
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia needs to address gaps across its maritime logistics and supply chain ecosystem to ensure its ports are able to handle rising cargo volumes driven by trade shift to the Asean region, said industry experts.
MTT Shipping and Logistics Bhd managing director and co-founder Ooi Lean Hin said Asean has emerged as one of the biggest beneficiaries of the trade shift, driven by supply chain realignments as China diversifies its market away from the West.
MORE TO COME
