Title: New law to replace Auku will exclude student matters, says Fahmi
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Any legislation replacing the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (Auku) will focus on university administration and management, while matters involving students and undergraduates will be excluded.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had informed the Cabinet today of the government's intention to abolish Auku.
He said Anwar also emphasised that student-related matters should not be included in any new legislation, as existing laws, including those involving the police, already applied to students.
"The prime minister has expressed his intention for the government to abolish Auku.
"At the same time, the prime minister said that although a new Bill may need to be introduced to regulate certain aspects of the administration and management of universities and university colleges, matters involving students and undergraduates should not be included in that legislation," he said at his weekly post-Cabinet media briefing today.
The Communications Minister said the Higher Education Ministry would identify the administrative aspects that needed to be regulated for universities and university colleges as institutions of higher education.
He said these would be prioritised in any legislation intended to replace selected provisions currently contained in Auku.
Anwar had previously announced plans to abolish Auku as part of efforts to strengthen academic freedom and university autonomy.
He said he opposed special laws specifically designed to restrict university students.
The plan has been welcomed by public university leaders as a transformative step towards strengthening institutional autonomy, governance and academic freedom.
They said the move demonstrated the government's commitment to comprehensive reform of the higher education ecosystem, while stressing that any new legal framework must strike a clear balance between freedom and accountability.
Universiti Malaysia Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah (UMPSA) vice-chancellor Professor Dr Yatimah Alias said the abolition should be viewed in a broader context, as the legislation governs university establishment, administration and overall governance, alongside student affairs.
Meanwhile, International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) rector Professor Emeritus Datuk Seri Dr Osman Bakar said the move would give students greater scope to develop mature thinking, strengthen their leadership potential and participate constructively in society.
Echoing this, Universiti Malaysia Terengganu (UMT) deputy vice-chancellor (Academic and International) and acting vice-chancellor Prof Dr Suriyani Muhamad described the repeal as a "golden opportunity" to clarify public university accountability.
Auku was originally introduced to regulate the establishment and administration of public universities and university colleges, but later became associated with restrictions on student activism and political activities on campuses, particularly following amendments in the mid-1970s.
The Act provides the legal framework for the establishment, governance and administration of public universities and university colleges in Malaysia.
It came into force on April 30, 1971, replacing the Emergency (Essential Powers) Ordinance No. 74, 1971, and remains the primary law governing public higher education institutions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kampar father, 2 daughters killed in Jalan Sultan Ismail crash identified
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The three family members killed in a crash involving an Immigration Department lorry along Jalan Sultan Ismail early today have been identified.
Kuala Lumpur Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the family was from Kampar, Perak.
The victims were identified as Shaik Mohd Firdaus Shaikh Yahya, 53, and his daughters, Siti Nor Sazlin, 25, and Siti Darwisyah Auni, 12.
Shaik Mohd Firdaus' wife, Norhayati Razali, 55, was seriously injured and is receiving treatment in the intensive care unit at Kuala Lumpur Hospital.
Another daughter, Siti Nor Shakira, 28, was not involved in the crash.
The
accident occurred at 1am at the Maju Junction traffic light intersection
and involved an Immigration Department lorry, a Proton Saga and an Inokom Matrix, as well as four pedestrians from the same family.
The Immigration lorry, driven by a 43-year-old man, allegedly ran a red light while its beacon lights and siren were activated before colliding with the Proton Saga.
The impact caused the lorry to lose control and hit the four pedestrians and the Inokom Matrix, which had stopped at the intersection.
The three victims died at the scene, while Norhayati suffered injuries to her head, right hand and both legs.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two UNHCR card holders charged over house break-ins
Article:
MUAR: Two Rohingya men linked to a string of house break-ins in the district were charged at the Magistrate's Court today.
Jamal Hussin Jalal, 30, and Ramzan Ali Ali, 31, both United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) cardholders, pleaded not guilty when the charges were read before Magistrate Muhammad Faizzudin Abd Ra'fik.
Jamal faced three charges while Ramzan faced one. They allegedly committed the offences while wearing masks and gloves.
Jamal was charged with trespassing into three houses with two other accomplices who remain at large.
The offences allegedly took place between 11.11pm and 3am on May 30, July 19 and July 21 at houses in Taman Sungai Abong Permai, Taman Temiang Jaya and Taman Permata Indah.
He was charged under Sections 447 and 448 of the Penal Code, which carry a maximum six-month jail term, a fine of up to RM3,000, or both upon conviction.
Meanwhile, Ramzan was charged with dishonestly retaining a stolen wristwatch at a house in Taman Peringgit Jaya, Melaka, at 1.30am on July 26.
The offence carries a maximum five-year jail term, a fine or both under Section 411 of the Penal Code.
Deputy public prosecutor Yasmin Mohd Piah prosecuted, while the accused were represented by lawyer Kelvinder Singh Sidhu.
The court granted Jamal bail of RM5,000 with two sureties for the first charge, RM1,500 with two sureties for the second and RM2,500 with two sureties for the third.
Ramzan was granted RM4,000 bail with two sureties.
The cases will be mentioned on Sept 22 for document submission.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lotte Chemical Titan neither confirms nor denies parent's potential stake sale
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Lotte Chemical Titan Holding Bhd has neither confirmed nor denied reports that its South Korean parent is looking to sell its stake in the company, after news of the potential sale sent its shares up more than 30 per cent.
In a clarification filed with Bursa Malaysia, the company said Lotte Chemical Corp (LCC), which owns 75 per cent of Lotte Chemical Titan, is considering various strategic measures concerning the company, but has made no decision thus far.
"We wish to clarify that after making due enquiry, we understand that LCC is considering various strategic measures related to the company without making any decision thus far," it said.
This comes after local news outlets citing Korea Economic Daily reported that Korea Exchange-listed LCC was revisiting plans to dispose of its interest in Lotte Chemical Titan, along with a partial divestment of an Indonesian unit.
Lotte Chemical Titan said it will make the necessary announcement as required under Bursa Malaysia's Main Market Listing Requirements should there be any further developments.
Earlier, shares of the Main Market-listed petrochemical producer surged as much as 30.65 per cent in early trade following reports of the potential stake sale.
The stock opened one sen, or 3.23 per cent, higher at 32 sen before climbing as much as 9.5 sen to 40.5 sen, its intraday high as at 2.45pm.
At the time of writing, the stock was trading at a more than two-month high of 37 sen, up 5.5 sen, or 17.74 per cent, with 30.81 million shares changing hands, its busiest trading day in more than four months.
The Korea Economic Daily report said Lotte Chemical Titan was the primary target for disposal, with LCC reviewing market conditions and potential buyers.
The South Korean group was also reportedly considering a partial divestment of its Indonesian petrochemical operations as it seeks to reduce its exposure to basic petrochemicals and expand into higher-margin speciality materials.
Lotte Chemical Titan has been loss-making for more than four years amid a prolonged downturn in the petrochemical industry.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysian passport ranked fourth strongest globally
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian passport has been ranked the fourth strongest in the world, with holders granted visa-free, visa-on-arrival or electronic travel authorisation access to 174 destinations.
According to data published by independent platform Passport Reports, Malaysia's passport is the second strongest in Asean and the third strongest in Asia.
It said the Malaysian passport scored a Global Mobility Score of 174, granting holders access to 87.9 per cent of the 199 countries evaluated without requiring a traditional visa in advance.
"Of these, 121 destinations, or 61.1 per cent, offer Malaysians visa-free entry.
"These include most of Europe, as well as key international destinations such as Japan, China, Singapore, Thailand, the United Arab Emirates, Brazil, Mexico, Australia and South Africa," it said in a statement today.
It said 45 destinations offer visa-on-arrival or simplified entry procedures, including Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, India, Maldives and South Sudan.
The report said Malaysian passport holders have access to eight destinations via electronic travel authorisation or equivalent digital systems, including the United Kingdom, Australia, South Korea, New Zealand and Seychelles.
Only 24 destinations, or 12.1 per cent of those assessed, require Malaysian passport holders to obtain a traditional visa or prior approval before travel.
These include the United States, Canada, North Korea, China's neighbouring nations such as Pakistan and Afghanistan, as well as several African nations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cigarettes hidden in coconut husks: Kelantan Customs foils RM1.37mil smuggling attempt
Article:
RANTAU PANJANG: The Kelantan Customs Department has foiled an attempt to smuggle 1.96 million sticks of cigarettes believed to have been brought in from China, with the total value of the seizure, including duties and taxes, estimated at RM1.37 million.
Kelantan Customs director Mohd Hisham Mohd Nor said the seizure was made by the Rantau Panjang Enforcement Branch Operations Team in Bachok on July 17 under Ops Asap Cino.
He said the team first detected an unlocked Hino lorry abandoned at Kampung Pauh 9, Tawang, around 10.30pm.
"An inspection of the lorry found white sacks containing coconut husks, which were used to conceal boxes containing cigarettes of various brands suspected to be smuggled.
"Further inspection led to the seizure of 1.7 million sticks of cigarettes of various brands packed in 74 boxes, with an estimated value of RM1.2 million, including duties and taxes," he said at a press conference at the Customs Enforcement Complex in Rantau Panjang here today.
Hisham said the team also detected a Toyota Unser at the same location carrying 253,600 sticks of white cigarettes, estimated to be worth RM178,027.20, including duties and taxes.
Two vehicles estimated to be worth RM165,000 were also seized.
The case is being investigated under Section 135(1)(e) of the Customs Act 1967.
Those convicted could be fined not less than 10 times the value of the goods or RM100,000, whichever is greater, and not more than 20 times the value of the goods or RM500,000, whichever is greater.
They could also face imprisonment for between 6 months and 5 years, or both, for a first offence.
He said the syndicate's modus operandi involved transporting the cigarettes by boat via the Sungai Golok before transferring the goods several times to other boats.
"All the cigarettes were intended for the market outside Kelantan and were believed to be in high demand among foreign construction workers," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Defending our sovereignty beyond the battlefield
Article:
IT is tempting to think of independence as a chapter closed 68 years ago, a date in a textbook rather than a duty still being carried out.
But sovereignty was never a one-time achievement. It must be renewed and defended by every generation, and the threats it faces today look nothing like those our founding fathers confronted.
A purely territorial idea of sovereignty is no longer enough. Consider the threats a young Malaysian will actually face.
A cyberattack on a national utility or bank can paralyse daily life more quickly than any conventional incursion — launched from a laptop thousands of kilometres away with no visible flag.
Disinformation, often amplified by algorithms, can erode public trust and inflame racial or religious fault lines faster than any physical provocation.
Economic coercion, the quiet leverage of depending on a single trading partner or source of critical technology, can compromise a nation's freedom of action just as surely as an army at the border.
None of these threats respect the boundaries drawn on a map, or announce themselves with the courtesy of a declaration of war.
This is why the conversation Malaysia needs this Merdeka is not only about defence budgets and hardware, but about a broader definition of national resilience.
Food security is sovereignty, because a nation that cannot feed itself in a crisis can be pressured. Digital infrastructure is sovereignty, because control over data and connectivity is now as strategically vital as control over an airfield.
Social cohesion is sovereignty too, since a divided society is far easier to destabilise from within than any army could manage from without.
A civil servant who resists corruption defends sovereignty. A teacher who nurtures independent thought defends sovereignty. A citizen who refuses to be provoked by inflammatory rhetoric online defends sovereignty just as surely as a soldier on watch at the border.
None of this diminishes the importance of a modern, well-equipped armed forces, nor the diplomatic skill needed to navigate a contested regional order.
Malaysia's geography, astride some of the busiest waterways in the world, means hard power and credible deterrence remain indispensable.
But hard power alone cannot secure a nation. True sovereignty depends not only on the capacity to defend a nation's borders, but on the character to preserve its unity from within.
As Malaysia marks another Merdeka, the most fitting tribute to the generation of 1957 is not nostalgia but renewal, the recognition that independence must be actively chosen and protected by each generation.
Selamat Hari Merdeka. May every Malaysian remain a sentry for the nation.
NEVHAN PHRASSANTHA NAIDU PUSPAKARAN
Alumni, National Defence University Malaysia (UPNM)
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt withdraws nicotine appeal, cites existing vape regulations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Control of Smoking Products for Public Health Act provides a sufficient legal framework to regulate the sale and use of nicotine-containing vape products, Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said.
He said this was among the main reasons for the government's decision to discontinue its appeal against a High Court ruling regarding the removal of nicotine from the poisons list.
"The decision to withdraw the appeal is also in line with the policy and direction of the Health Ministry, which is responsible for championing public health," he said in a statement today.
Dusuki said the decision was made after Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad studied the High Court's grounds of judgment.
The minister decided on Aug 13 not to pursue the appeal after considering arguments raised by the applicants in their judicial review, including the previous lack of legal provisions regulating the sale and use of nicotine vape liquids to minors under 18.
The Attorney-General's Chambers filed the notice of discontinuance at the Court of Appeal today.
The withdrawal means the High Court's ruling that the government's decision to remove liquid nicotine from the poisons list was irrational and made without proper or adequate consultation with the Poisons Board remains in force.
On May 15, High Court judge Datuk Aliza Sulaiman ruled that exempting nicotine from the poisons list under the Poisons (Amendment of Poisons List) Order 2023 was irrational and ultra vires Section 6 of the Poisons Act 1952.
The judicial review was brought by the Malaysian Council for Tobacco Control, the Malaysian Green Lung Association, and Voice of the Children to declare the directive null and void.
On April 1, 2023, the Health Ministry had published a gazette notice stating that nicotine liquids and gels used in e-cigarettes and vape products had been granted exemption from poisons control.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fahmi: New legislation to replace UUCA will exclude provisions affecting student freedom
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — The new legislation that will replace the Universities and University Colleges Act (UUCA) 1971 will not restrict the freedom of students or undergraduates.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil assured that the new legislative Bill will instead focus on the administration and management aspects of universities as well as university colleges.
He said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had told the Cabinet that matters involving students and undergraduates will be excluded following the government’s intention to abolish UUCA 1971 as announced last weekend.
“With that, the Higher Education Ministry has announced that the aspects that need to be managed involve the administration of universities and university colleges as higher education institutions,” he said in the weekly media post-Cabinet briefing that was broadcast live today.
Fahmi, who is also the communications minister, however, said laws involving the police and other authorities still apply.
He explained that existing laws, including those involving authorities such as the police, will still apply to students and undergraduates.
Last Saturday, it was reported that Anwar, when delivering his presidential policy speech at the 2026 PKR national congress in Melaka, announced that the government would abolish UUCA 1971.
Anwar, who was speaking as the PKR president, said that although several amendments had been made before, there were still things that did not satisfy the undergraduates.
The UUCA 1971 was introduced to govern the establishment, governance and administration of public universities and university colleges in Malaysia.
However, it was later seen to be restrictive to student freedom and activism.

Title: Finance Ministry witness says PMO involved in Jana Wibawa procurement process, but no order to select KCJ Engineering
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — The Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) was involved in the government’s procurement process for the Jana Wibawa programme by submitting a list of 54 proposed contractors and later providing additional information that led the Finance Ministry to re-evaluate a Bumiputera contractor that had initially failed its assessment, the High Court heard today.
The Finance Ministry’s deputy secretary-general (policy) Datuk Zamzuri Abdul Aziz confirmed this while testifying as the 26th prosecution witness in former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s power abuse and money laundering trial.
Today, Zamzuri referred to Muhyiddin’s November 13, 2020 letter to the finance minister, which contained a list of 54 proposed companies for 54 proposed Jana Wibawa projects, including KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd.
At that time, Zamzuri was secretary of the Finance Ministry’s government procurement division.
When asked by lead prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin, Zamzuri said the list was from the letter signed by Muhyiddin, but was uncertain about how this list was created.
Based on this list, Zamzuri agreed that the PMO was involved before the process to evaluate contractors for three of the Jana Wibawa projects, which were eventually awarded to KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, Nepturis Sdn Bhd and Sutracom Sdn Bhd.
In this trial, evidence had shown that KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd was on July 30, 2021 given a RM62 million contract under Jana Wibawa via direct negotiation or without going through an open tender to build a road from Felda Bukit Jalor to Gemas, Negeri Sembilan.
Banking evidence had previously also shown that KCJ Engineering later, on September 1, 2022, issued RM800,000 in cheques to Muhyiddin’s political party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia.
On October 12, 2022, KCJ Engineering’s RM800,000 cheques entered Bersatu’s CIMB bank account.
Following the PMO’s letter containing the 54 proposed Jana Wibawa contractors to the Finance Ministry, Zamzuri had directed his then deputy, Datin Rosni Mohd Yusoff, to carry out evaluations on whether the contractors were qualified for the Jana Wibawa projects.
Zamzuri confirmed that KCJ Engineering had initially failed the Finance Ministry’s evaluation and that this would usually result in the company not being considered for government projects.
He said he did not know why the PMO gave additional information on KCJ Engineering on February 3, 2021, but agreed that this showed the PMO was involved in the government procurement process.
Based on the additional information from the PMO, Zamzuri replied yes when Wan Shaharuddin asked if there “was involvement in the procurement process by PMO”.
Yesterday, Rosni said KCJ Engineering had initially failed the Finance Ministry’s evaluation as it had a record of having sick projects and unsatisfactory work performance, but cleared a second round of evaluations based on additional information from the PMO on February 3, 2021.
Earlier, Zamzuri agreed with Muhyiddin’s lawyer Chetan Jethwani that the PMO had provided the Finance Ministry with a list of additional information on multiple companies, instead of just KCJ Engineering.
Zamzuri agreed that the PMO would not have sent so much additional information if the Finance Ministry did not request more information, also agreeing that the request for additional information was because of incomplete information for the evaluation of contractors.
Chetan: And at no time did PMO or Tan Sri (Muhyiddin) say to you or anyone in the government procurement division that you have to select KCJ Engineering even though they have failed, there is no interference of that nature?
Zamzuri: Correct.
Zamzuri agreed with Chetan that this was a normal process of re-evaluation for all contractors since the project was via direct negotiation, where only one contractor is involved.
In this trial, Muhyiddin is facing seven charges, namely four counts of alleged power abuse to obtain RM225.3 million in bribes for his party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd), and three counts of alleged money laundering involving money that Bersatu received from Bukhary Equity.
The trial before High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin resumes tomorrow.

Title: Police probe whether stress played role in Hulu Selangor teacher’s death
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 19 — Police are continuing investigations into the death of a female teacher who was found unconscious at a school in Hulu Selangor late last month.
Selangor Police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said investigators were examining various factors, including whether stress played a role, in the case which has so far been classified as a sudden death report (SDR).
“Statements have been taken from several individuals, including the deceased’s colleagues, as we want to establish the cause.
“As I have said, the investigation is not yet complete. There are still many people we need to call in to verify information,” he told a press conference on the Selangor Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department’s operations today.
Media reports previously said the teacher was found unconscious at a school in Hulu Selangor on July 31 and later pronounced dead while receiving treatment in hospital.
Separately, Shazeli said police were investigating allegations that a workshop in Kampung Bukit Kapar, Klang, which had been linked to foreign nationals suspected of dismantling and selling vehicle parts, was set on fire to destroy evidence.
“At this stage, I am not entirely convinced it is a syndicate because only two foreign nationals, the owner and an employee, have been arrested.
“However, we cannot rule out the possibility of a wider syndicate operating elsewhere, with the premises merely used to dismantle the vehicles. We are also investigating the landowner to determine why the property was rented to foreign nationals,” he said.
Police previously arrested a foreign man in his 20s to assist investigations after a hearse believed to have been stolen was found at a used-vehicle workshop in Bukit Kapar at about 7.20pm on August 7.
The Immigration Department also detained 20 foreign nationals, comprising 19 men and one woman, in a raid on Jalan Kapar at about 4.30pm on August 12.
The raid uncovered an operation allegedly involved in dismantling and selling stolen vehicles, including a multi-purpose vehicle belonging to a funeral management company that had been reported missing.
The detention of Indonesian nationals during the raid also uncovered suspected involvement in operating a “safe house” for undocumented migrants awaiting repatriation. — Bernama

Title: Sandakan declares fire disaster after 28 homes destroyed on Pulau Nunuyan Laut
Article:
SANDAKAN, Aug 19 — The Sandakan District Disaster Management Committee (JPBD) today declared a fire disaster in the district following a blaze that destroyed 28 houses at Pulau Nunuyan Laut early this morning.
Sandakan JPBD chairman Datuk Walter Kenson said the declaration was made at 9am based on reports and information received from agencies on the ground.
In a statement here today, he said a temporary relief centre (PPS) was opened at Masjid Al Fattah, Kampung Nunuyan Laut, at 10am following the declaration.
He said the centre was activated after the affected homes were deemed unsafe for occupation, with registration of victims currently underway. — Bernama

Title: Haze eases for now, but could return within days, says MetMalaysia
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 19 — Humid weather over the past few days has helped ease haze in the Klang Valley and Sarawak, but conditions could deteriorate again in the near future.
Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said hot and dry conditions were expected to return within days, with the country still in the Southwest Monsoon season until the end of September.
“The risk of haze remains as long as the Southwest Monsoon winds persist,” he told Bernama.
During the Southwest Monsoon, lower humidity contributes to reduced rainfall and more days without rain, Mohd Hisham said.
He said the country’s haze conditions were also being influenced by El Niño, which is currently moderate but is expected to intensify between October and December.
“These two factors combined are contributing to drier conditions and a higher risk of forest and peatland fires, which could trigger local and transboundary haze,” he said.
According to Mohd Hisham, meteorological analysis, Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) hotspot data, atmospheric modelling, the Malaysian Community Multiscale Air Quality model and wind trajectory analysis indicated that the haze in the Klang Valley had local causes, while the haze affecting parts of Sarawak was linked to both local and transboundary factors.
He said the monitoring was supported by satellite imagery from the ASMC and weather information shared by neighbouring countries.
“Weather model analysis also showed winds consistently blowing from areas with a high concentration of hotspots in western Borneo towards southern Sarawak,” he said.
As of this morning, five areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings.
Data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal showed that Serian recorded the highest reading at 156, followed by Kuching (154), Sri Aman (152), Samarahan (113), and Mukah (106).
Meanwhile, 58 areas across the country recorded moderate API readings of between 51 and 100, while five areas recorded good air quality (readings below 50).
Yesterday, Mohd Hisham reportedly said the likelihood of El Niño reaching the very strong or “Super El Niño” category from October to December had exceeded 90 per cent and could make it one of the most extreme on record.
He said the strong El Niño episode was likely to coincide with a positive Indian Ocean Dipole, which could exacerbate the decline in rainfall across the region. — Bernama

Title: ‘No need to escalate’: Selangor police urge public against gathering at court over Rocky case
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 19 — Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar today reportedly urged the public not to hold a gathering when a man linked to the death of a dog named Rocky appears in court tomorrow, saying the legal process is already under way.
According to
The Star
, Shazeli said police had completed their investigation, identified those responsible and received instructions for charges to be brought.
“There is no need to escalate this issue to the extent of organising any gathering or demonstration,” he was quoted as saying.
He reportedly said members of the public who wished to witness the proceedings could attend as the court’s public gallery would be open.
He added that the case showed police had neither ignored the matter nor taken sides.
Lawyer Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali earlier said his client, Muhammad Shah Hizam, 24, had been served a summons by a Department of Veterinary Services officer to appear in court at 9am tomorrow, although the exact charge has yet to be disclosed.
The Malaysian Stray Animal Association previously alleged that a group of men beat and strangled Rocky in Taman Teluk Gedung Indah, Port Klang, on July 29, despite pleas from the dog’s owner for it to be released.

Title: KL police identify father and two daughters killed in Maju Junction crash; nephew says family was visiting relatives
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Police have identified the three family members killed in the early morning crash involving a Malaysian Immigration Department lorry on Jalan Sultan Ismail.
Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief ACP Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said they were Shaik Mohd Firdaus Shaikh Yahya, 53, and his two daughters, Siti Nor Sazlin, 25, and Siti Darwisyah Auni, 12.
“Shaik Mohd Firdaus’ 55-year-old wife is being treated in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) of Kuala Lumpur Hospital,” he said when contacted today.
He added that the Immigration lorry driver and Proton Saga driver, aged 43 and 50, have been remanded for one day until tomorrow to assist with investigations.
Meanwhile, Shaik Mohd Firdaus’ nephew, Zaid Darfis, 39, said his uncle had come to Kuala Lumpur to visit his mother in Semenyih, Selangor.
“He managed to call my mother-in-law to inform us the family had arrived in Kuala Lumpur. I only found out about the accident after she called me around 7.30 this morning,” he said.
A Bernama check at the National Institute of Forensic Medicine of the hospital found family members and relatives of the victims still gathered at the hospital. Also present was Kuala Lumpur Immigration director Hamsha Injau.
It is understood that the victims’ remains will be taken to Masjid Jamiul Ehsan, Jalan Pahang for prayers and funeral rites before being laid to rest at the Muslim cemetery in Kampung Air Hitam Labu, Kampar, Perak.
The crash occurred around 1 am, when an empty Isuzu Black Maria Immigration lorry was believed to be travelling from the Kuala Lumpur Immigration Office to Chow Kit for an operation against undocumented migrants.
It apparently entered the Maju Junction intersection while the traffic light at its lane was red, with its beacon lights and siren activated. At the same time, a Proton Saga moving straight on a green light was reportedly unable to avoid the lorry and collided with it.
The impact sent the lorry careering out of control and into a skid, mowing down four pedestrians, who were members of the same family, along with an Inokom Matrix multi-purpose vehicle.
Three of the pedestrians, a 53-year-old man and his two daughters, aged 25 and 12, were killed at the scene. The mother, aged 55, was severely injured.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987. — Bernama

Title: Ahead of Budget 2027, higher education students call for expanded assistance to manage rising living expenses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Ahead of the tabling of Budget 2027, higher education students are hoping the government will expand financial assistance to help them cope with rising costs of living.
Besides increases to existing aid such as Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA), students are calling for new measures to ease their daily expenses.
Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) Shah Alam Students’ Representative Council member Muhammad Ammar Romli, 22, said initiatives such as book vouchers and Menu Siswa Rahmah had made a positive impact but were insufficient to cover food, transport, accommodation and academic expenses.
“Food assistance such as Menu Siswa Rahmah has a significant impact because it directly reduces students’ daily expenses, but there is still considerable room for improvement,” he told Bernama.
Increasing National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) loans was not a complete solution, he said, calling on the government to provide targeted assistance or subsidies to help cover education and living costs without adding to students’ financial burden after graduation.
Universiti Selangor (UNISEL) student Abhinaayasri Srivenkatarao shared similar concerns, saying that while the Madani Government had introduced various initiatives to support students, the high cost of living remained a burden.
“PTPTN loans are very helpful, but for some students they are no longer enough to cover education and living expenses,” she said.
Parents also described financing higher education as a major challenge, particularly for families with several children still studying.
Zareah Kandam, 49, said families faced significant pressure from tuition fees, educational supplies and their children’s daily expenses.
“The burden is greater for families with more than one child studying at a higher education institution.
“Government initiatives such as education loans, scholarships, financial assistance and subsidies have certainly helped, but some families still need additional support, particularly as living costs continue to rise,” she said.
Zareah hoped Budget 2027 would introduce more comprehensive measures, including financial assistance for students enrolling at university, hostel fee subsidies and higher living allowances.
“Transport assistance would also greatly help students studying far from home. The application process for aid should be simplified and take into account household income and the number of children pursuing higher education,” she said.
Student welfare has also emerged as a prominent topic on social media platform Threads, with users calling on the government to pay greater attention to students’ financial struggles.
The government has previously introduced initiatives including Madani Book Vouchers, MySiswa Job On Campus and Ikhtiar Dapur Siswa Madani to support students.
Budget 2027 is scheduled to be tabled in Parliament on October 9. — Bernama

Title: Shah Alam police receive report on Form Three student at risk of hearing loss after alleged bullying
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 19 — Police have confirmed receiving a report regarding an incident involving a Form Three student who claimed to have been bullied to the extent of being at risk of hearing loss at a secondary school here last week.
Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the 17-year-old suspect had been detained and released on police bail pending completion of investigations.
“The investigation is still ongoing, and statements have been recorded. The incident is believed to have stemmed from teasing between schoolmates.
“As for the extent of the injuries, I cannot comment as we have to wait for the official report from the medical officer,” he told a press conference on the achievements of the Selangor contingent’s Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) here today.
Shazeli said the case was being investigated under Sections 506 and 323 of the Penal Code.
Yesterday, the media reported that a Form Three male student had suffered injuries to his neck and nape and was at risk of hearing loss after allegedly being bullied and assaulted at a secondary school here last week.
More distressingly, the incident also left the 15-year-old victim severely traumatised, causing him to spend much of his time confined to his room, besides experiencing a loss of appetite and speaking less. — Bernama

Title: Quizzed on China-Taiwan relations, Anwar says he would use force if needed to prevent Malaysia from breaking up (VIDEO)
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 19 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim believes he would use force to prevent any province from breaking away from the Federation of Malaysia.
In a special interview titled ‘Malaysia between the superpowers’ with Sreenivasan Jain for
Al Jazeera
’s programme ‘
A Changing World? The Contest for Global Powe
r’, which aired on August 16, Anwar said force should be used to protect territorial integrity.
He was using Malaysia as an example when asked if China should be condemned if it resorted to using force should the country fail to achieve peaceful reunification with Taiwan.
https://www.facebook.com/borneopost.online/videos/in-al-jazeera-interview-datuk-seri-anwar-ibrahim-says-hell-use-force-to-prevent-/1877609623645151/
Sreenivasan: China has said that if peaceful reunification doesn’t work, they reserve the right to use force if it comes to that. Would you condemn that?
Anwar: I always take it, Malaysia as an example. If one province decides, yes, to break away. Do we use force?  I think I will (to) protect the sanctity and unity of the nation.
Sreenivasan: So, you would use force?
Anwar: Yes. Because otherwise they’ll be fragmented.
His remarks came as the interview examined what he described as growing hypocrisy among Western countries and superpowers in applying international principles.
“I said that this hypocrisy cannot be tolerated,” Anwar said, when asked about his criticism of Western superpowers.
The exchange took place against the backdrop of what the programme described as the weakening of the existing international order and increasing rivalry between major powers.
Anwar has repeatedly advocated an independent Malaysian foreign policy, arguing that the country should not be forced to choose between competing power centres such as the United States and China, while maintaining its position on issues of justice and international law.
The interview also touched on Anwar’s criticism of Western powers over the Gaza conflict and his broader contention that major powers should be held to the same principles and international rules they expect others to observe. — The Borneo Post

Title: Xavier Jayakumar corruption probe closed in 2024 due to insufficient evidence, says MACC
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 19 — A corruption investigation involving former minister Datuk Dr Xavier Jayakumar reportedly was closed in 2024 after prosecutors found insufficient evidence to charge him, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) said today.
Utusan Malaysia
reported that MACC said two investigation papers had been opened in 2021 under Section 16(a)(A) of the MACC Act 2009, with the relevant facts, documents and evidence subsequently examined.
“The deputy public prosecutor decided to classify the case as ‘closed and filed’ in 2024 because there was insufficient evidence to charge Datuk Dr Xavier,” the commission was quoted as saying.
The disclosure came a day after former Petaling Jaya MP Kua Kia Soong questioned the status of the investigation, saying there had been no public confirmation of its outcome.
It also comes shortly after Xavier confirmed his return to PKR, five years after quitting the party in 2021 and subsequently supporting then prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s administration as an independent MP.
At the time of his departure from PKR, Xavier was being investigated by MACC following the detention of his close associate M A Thinagaran over suspected bribes linked to projects awarded by the Water, Land and Natural Resources Ministry in 2019, when Xavier headed the ministry.
MACC urged the public not to speculate about the case, saying investigations were conducted based on the available facts and evidence and that the time required depended on the complexity of each case.

Title: Melaka Sentral refutes claim terminal has been without air‑conditioning for months
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 19 — Melaka Sentral Sdn Bhd (MSSB) has denied claims that the terminal has been operating without air-conditioning for more than three months, as recently circulated on social media.
Its general manager Zulhafni Md Rahis said records and monitoring showed that the temperature inside the terminal remained under control.
He said MSSB regularly monitors and maintains the air-conditioning system to ensure the comfort of visitors and smooth terminal operations.
“We are always open to complaints and feedback from traders and visitors regarding comfort and facilities at the terminal. Complaints can be submitted through the complaint forms provided or via the Public Complaints Management System (SISPAA) for the management’s attention and action,” he said in a statement here today.
Zulhafni said all complaints would be reviewed and appropriate action taken according to established procedures, with feedback provided within 10 working days.
He also urged the public to obtain information and clarification from the management before making statements about the terminal’s operations and facilities to ensure accurate information was conveyed.
Zulhafni said MSSB remained committed to ensuring the terminal’s facilities and services were well maintained for users’ comfort and safety. — Bernama

Title: KL police say personal grudge behind petrol attack on woman at Kepong lottery outlet
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Police believe a personal grudge was behind an incident in which a man allegedly poured petrol on a woman and set her alight at a lottery outlet in Taman Pusat Kepong on August 9.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Comm Datuk Fadil Marsus said this when confirming details of the case, according to a report by
The Star.
He said officers arrested a 59-year-old local man in Kepong yesterday to assist investigations.
Comm Fadil said initial findings indicated that “the motive was a personal grudge linked to lottery numbers,” adding that the suspect and victim were not related but knew each other.
“We will apply for a remand order against the suspect today to assist in investigations,” he added.
He said the victim, a 62-year-old counter attendant, suffered burns to about 50 per cent of her body and remains hospitalised under sedation.
He said police received a call at about 8am on the day of the incident reporting that a woman had been attacked by an unidentified man, as previously stated by Acting Sentul OCPD Supt Jasni Zolpa.
He said the case remains under investigation.

Title: Works Ministry seeks bigger 2027 development budget to bolster infrastructure plans, says Ahmad Maslan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — The Ministry of Works (KKR) is seeking a higher allocation in the 2027 Budget compared with the previous year to ensure the nation’s infrastructure development agenda continues to be strengthened.
Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan said the ministry hoped to remain one of the main recipients of Development Expenditure (DE) allocations in the government’s annual budget.
“Year after year, out of the 28 ministries, KKR receives the largest development allocation. For instance, in 2026, out of a total DE allocation of RM81 billion, nearly RM9.6 billion, or 10 per cent, was allocated to KKR.
“So, we hope to maintain this leading position in terms of DE. We have indeed requested a higher allocation than last year, but we leave the final decision to the Ministry of Finance. We understand that they may face certain constraints, such as rising subsidy costs,” he said.
He said this at a press conference after officiating the pre-launch of the 13th Malaysian Road Conference and Exhibition 2026 and the 6th International Road Federation Global Asia-Pacific Regional Congress here today.
Ahmad said the matter was among the topics discussed during his meeting yesterday in Putrajaya with Second Finance Minister Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan and Treasury Secretary-General Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican.
Commenting on the conference, he said it would provide broader opportunities to showcase and advance local road engineering technology and innovation on the international stage.
He said the conference, themed “Transforming the Nation Through Future Ready Roads”, reflected Malaysia’s commitment to developing road infrastructure that is resilient, sustainable and aligned with future development needs.
“A total of 111 exhibition booths will be set up during the conference to showcase the latest products and technologies from relevant sectors.
“We are also targeting an attendance of 1,000 participants from both within and outside the country, with 100 technical paper presenters sharing their experiences in engineering technology and innovation,” he said.
The international-standard conference and exhibition will be held from October 13 to 15 at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur (WTCKL). — Bernama

Title: Consular assistance to Malaysians detained abroad does not grant immunity, says legal expert
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Malaysians are reminded that consular assistance provided by Malaysian embassies or High Commissions to citizens detained abroad does not grant them immunity from the laws of the host country.
Instead, the consular role is to ensure that the detainees’ welfare and rights are protected, said Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Shah Alam, Faculty of Law, Advocacy and Dispute Resolution Centre head Mimi Sintia Mohd Bajury.
“The consular function is to safeguard the detainee’s wellbeing, help contact their families and facilitate access to legal aid.
“Consular officials also monitor court proceedings to uphold the accused’s right to a fair trial, in accordance with the host country’s laws.
“Being a foreign national does not mean a person can be denied their basic rights,” she said today during Bernama TV’s FOKUS 15 programme titled ‘Crossing Borders: The Legal Rights of Citizens from an International Perspective’.
Mimi Sintia highlighted that Malaysians detained or investigated overseas have rights under international law, including the right to be informed of the reason for their detention, access to legal counsel, fair treatment and consular assistance.
“Malaysian passports only establish citizenship. However, when we are in another country, such as Singapore, Indonesia, or Thailand, our actions are subject to their laws,” she said.
She also advised Malaysians travelling or conducting business abroad to understand and comply with the laws of the countries they visit, and also not to carry items on behalf of strangers.
“It is important for Malaysian travellers abroad to know local laws and available support channels to ensure their safety and rights are protected,” she added. — Bernama

Title: KL police dispose of RM15m in seized drugs to ensure integrity of case exhibits
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — The Kuala Lumpur police today disposed of various types of drugs worth over RM15 million seized during operations across the capital, as part of efforts to ensure the integrity and proper management of case exhibits.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the disposal involved 5,022 case exhibits from 4,884 investigation papers for which court proceedings had concluded between 2007 and 2025.
“This disposal is not merely about destroying drugs, it serves to break the chain of abuse, eliminate avenues for leakage, and reaffirm that every seizure designated as a case exhibit will be disposed of in a direct, controlled and transparent manner,” he said.
He said this at a press conference following the Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department’s drug exhibit disposal ceremony at the Kuala Lumpur Police Headquarters here today.
Fadil said the solid drugs disposed of totalled 544 kilogrammes, comprising methamphetamine, ketamine, heroin, cocaine and cannabis, while liquid drugs exceeded 900 litres, including ketum liquid.
“All these cases involve offences under Sections 39B, 39A(2), 39A(1) and 6 of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, as well as Sections 12(2) and 33 of the Poisons Act 1952 for cases involving ketum liquid,” he said.
Fadil said the open disposal process also aimed to dispel negative perceptions and public misconceptions about how authorities manage large quantities of seized drugs.
“We aim to avoid public misconceptions regarding the seizure of these hundreds of kilogrammes of material. Today’s disposal demonstrates that established procedures are in place to ensure the integrity of case exhibits is maintained,” he said.
He said the destruction process was carried out in accordance with the Inspector-General of Police’s Standing Order (PTKPN) D207, in collaboration with Quality Alam Sdn Bhd, using Scheduled Waste-to-Energy technology at an incineration plant in Bukit Pelandok, Negeri Sembilan.
He added that the method also helped reduce health and safety risks to personnel arising from prolonged exposure to hazardous chemicals. — Bernama

Title: Firefighters save 162 homes after blaze destroys 28 stilt houses at Pulau Nunuyan Laut in Sandakan
Article:
SANDAKAN, Aug 19 — A total of 28 non-permanent stilt houses were destroyed in a fire at Kampung Nunuyan Laut, Nunuyan Laut Island, here early today.
The Sabah Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations Centre, in a statement, said no injuries or fatalities were reported in the incident.
“The Fire and Rescue Department received an emergency call at 3.50am and subsequently deployed the Sandakan Fire and Rescue Station team, assisted by a Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) boat, to the scene, located 18 kilometres away.
“The fire was brought under control at 5.45am, and the team’s swift action saved 162 nearby houses from being affected,” read the statement.
The journey to the scene involved a six-kilometre land route from the Sandakan Fire Station to the Maritime Jetty, followed by a 12-kilometre journey by an MMEA boat. — Bernama

Title: Police receive 375 tactical e‑bikes worth RM8m for faster, quieter border patrols
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) has received 375 All Terrain Tactical Assault E-Bikes (ATEBs) worth more than RM8 million to strengthen security along the country’s borders.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the electric tactical bikes would be deployed to states bordering Thailand, including Perlis, Kedah, Kelantan and Perak, as well as Sabah and Sarawak.
He said the ATEBs would enhance the capabilities of police personnel, particularly the General Operations Force (GOF), allowing them to conduct border patrols more quickly, quietly and effectively.
“At the same time, tackling leakages, particularly involving petrol and other goods, remains a priority to ensure they do not occur at the border.
“This will help ensure that government revenue is maintained at the highest possible level,” he told reporters after a ceremony to receive the vehicles today.
Also present were Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department director Datuk Seri Mohd Yusri Hassan Basri and RTG Intech Corporation Sdn Bhd management director Mohamad Roslan Ramin.
Mohd Khalid thanked RTG, the supplier of ATEBs, and expressed hope that the strategic partnership would continue to enhance the force’s operational capabilities.
The electric bikes can reach a top speed of 120km/h, deliver up to 850 Newton-metres (Nm) of torque and have an operating range of up to 120km.
They are also equipped with smart chargers and 72-volt, 60-ampere-hour batteries designed for demanding police operations.
The bikes will make their first public appearance during the upcoming National Day parade. — Bernama

Title: Malaysians among applicants affected as Australia slows Work and Holiday visa processing
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Australia has temporarily paused applications from Malaysians seeking their first Work and Holiday visa under subclass 462.
Australia’s
ABC News
reported yesterday that Malaysia is among 24 countries — almost all under visa stream — whose applications have been paused.
Australian Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke reportedly said the visas were “being processed more slowly than they were previously”, but did not give further details on the change.
The subclass 462 visa allows eligible Malaysians aged 18 to 30 to spend 12 months in Australia for short-term work and study, with Malaysia allocated an annual grant cap of 1,100 places.
The cap reportedly applies only to first subclass 462 visas, while second and third Work and Holiday visas are not subject to country quotas.
According to the report, Australia’s Department of Home Affairs said a country’s applications may be paused to spread lodgements throughout the programme year, when the country is close to reaching its annual grant cap, or to support the government’s broader migration settings.
The department reportedly did not say which of these reasons applies specifically to Malaysia.
Home Affairs reportedly said paused caps will reopen later in the same programme year and advised prospective applicants to monitor its website for changes.
ABC
also reported that some people who had already lodged working holiday visa applications in early July were still awaiting decisions by mid-August amid slower processing.
Experts interviewed by
ABC
suggested the slowdown could be linked to Australia’s wider efforts to manage net overseas migration.

Title: Kelantan police vow firm action against ‘tonto’ used to block enforcement in human‑smuggling cases
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Aug 19 — Police will take firm action against human-smuggling syndicates using ‘tonto’ to obstruct enforcement vehicles, following a recent incident in which two General Operations Force (GOF) personnel were hit while carrying out their duties.
Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the incident showed that the syndicates were becoming increasingly bold, stressing that such actions would not be tolerated.
“Human smuggling is a serious issue. They were willing to hit GOF personnel, which is an outrageous act that should not have happened,” he told a press conference at the Kelantan Police Contingent Headquarters (IPK) here today.
He said action would be taken against all parties involved under the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007 (ATIPSOM), as well as Sections 353 and 186 of the Penal Code.
Mohd Yusoff said police had also detected human-smuggling activities using sea routes and rivers along the Kelantan coast, adding that enforcement agencies would remain vigilant against such operations.
He said the incident involving the GOF personnel was still considered an isolated case, but urged officers operating in the field, particularly GOF members and the Kelantan IPK task force, to remain alert and take appropriate action within the law when faced with threats.
On Aug 15, a land-based smuggler transporting six undocumented Myanmar women rammed two GOF personnel during an inspection at Kampung Chat Palekbang, Tumpat, before being arrested. — Bernama

Title: Immigration Dept opens internal probe after fatal KL crash that killed three
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — The Immigration Department today confirmed that one of its vehicles was involved in a fatal road accident along Jalan Sultan Ismail here early this morning.
In a statement posted on Facebook, Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the department would give its full cooperation to the police in determining the cause of the accident.
“The department respects the ongoing investigation process and will not make any conclusions that could pre-empt the findings of the authorities,” he said.
Zakaria said the department would also conduct an internal investigation into compliance with standard operating procedures and safety aspects involving the operation of department vehicles to ensure the matter was thoroughly examined.
He urged those with information about the incident to assist the authorities, while asking the public to respect the privacy and sensitivities of the victims’ families and refrain from sharing unverified images, recordings or information.
Zakaria said the department viewed the incident seriously and would take appropriate action based on the findings of the police investigation and its internal probe.
The department also expressed its condolences and sympathy to the victims’ families and wished those receiving treatment a speedy recovery.

Title: MB: Pahang reports end of recorded hardcore poverty, with 2,913 households lifted and overall poverty down 30pc
Article:
KUANTAN, Aug 19 — Pahang’s hardcore poverty was brought to an end on Feb 19, with all 2,913 heads of household recorded in the Jan 15, 2026 figure removed from the status, said Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail.
He said the state had also recorded a 30 per cent reduction in poverty, with 4,263 of the 14,210 heads of household classified as poor on June 5 subsequently removed from the category.
“The classification is based on the 2024 Poverty Line published by the Department of Statistics Malaysia under the Ministry of Economy,” he said in a statement today.
Wan Rosdy said key factors behind the achievement included targeted assistance, initiatives and interventions provided by the state and federal governments and relevant agencies, as well as changes in household income and household size.
According to him, households with a monthly per capita income below RM372 in urban areas and RM345 in rural areas are classified as hardcore poor, while those earning less than RM790 and RM714 respectively are classified as poor.
Wan Rosdy said a family’s status could also change due to changes in income, job losses and changes in household size, including children moving out to get married or take up employment.
“This milestone does not mean our efforts to eradicate poverty have come to an end. On the contrary, it requires continued action, monitoring and intervention, with the state government continuing to strengthen its poverty reduction efforts to ensure the benefits of prosperity and wellbeing reach people throughout Pahang,” he said.
He said the state government would continue to collaborate with the federal government, aid agencies, local authorities, elected representatives, and community leaders to ensure that families classified as poor or hardcore poor in the eKasih household poverty database receive the assistance they need.
“Our goal is not just to lift people out of poverty, but to help them become self-reliant, secure more stable incomes and achieve a better quality of life,” he said. — Bernama

Title: More workplace subsidies, tax incentives needed to support breastfeeding mothers, says Yeo Bee Yin
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 19 — The government should provide more subsidies and tax incentives to companies to set up breastfeeding rooms and childcare facilities in the workplace.
Parliamentary Special Select Committee on Women, Children and Community Development chairman Yeo Bee Yin said such a move is necessary as many mothers find it challenging to continue breastfeeding after returning to work.
“In terms of the budget, as a Member of Parliament (for Puchong), I want more tax incentives for offices and companies to provide breastfeeding facilities.
“This includes breastfeeding rooms or multipurpose rooms where mothers can pump their milk, as well as childcare facilities in the workplace,” she said during a panel discussion titled ‘Realities of Breastfeeding’, held in conjunction with Toshiba Lifestyle Malaysia’s ‘World Breastfeeding Month 2026: Empowering Every Mother’s Journey’ event here yesterday.
Yeo launched the event, while the panel discussion, moderated by Nani Roslan, featured certified lactation consultant and infant care expert Elizabeth Richard and actress Natasha Hudson.
Yeo said breastfeeding and childcare issues often lacked sufficient attention in Parliament as women only made up about 13.5 per cent of the 222 Members of Parliament in Malaysia.
She emphasised that breastfeeding mothers required support from their families, employers and society, adding that they should not feel guilty when facing challenges such as low milk supply or breast engorgement.
“What children need most is a happy mother because that’s how they will grow up feeling safe and at peace. If you do not have enough milk or face difficulties, take it easy, seek treatment and take care of yourself,” she said.
Meanwhile, Elizabeth said mothers should refrain from self-blame when encountering breastfeeding difficulties as every baby is different, adding that those who cannot breastfeed directly could express and store their milk for their infants.
“Every child is different. A mother also learns new things with each child because their behaviour and her milk supply can be different. If you cannot breastfeed, it does not mean that you are a failure. You have tried, and there are other ways,” she said.
She added that those who are unable to breastfeed directly could express and store their milk for their infants, and that employers should be understanding of the time required for this process.
Actress and mother of five Natasha Hudson, 44, said she is still learning as every breastfeeding experience is different, noting that she had to combine breastfeeding with formula milk for the first time when her milk supply dropped while nursing her fourth daughter.
“I am always learning something new with every newborn. Even if I have experience, it does not mean that it will be the same because every child is different,” she said.
Natasha added that she received help from a lactation consultant while breastfeeding her fourth child and learned how to deal with mastitis, an inflammation of breast tissue that causes pain, swelling and redness. — Bernama

Title: Investment firm director previously charged with CBT now faces RM13.4m money‑laundering counts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — An investment company director, previously charged with criminal breach of trust, was brought before the Sessions Court here again today to face 10 charges of receiving RM13.4 million in proceeds from unlawful activities.
Datuk Norliza Tajudin, 54, pleaded not guilty after all the charges were read out individually before Judge Suzana Hussin.
She is charged with receiving the money through cheques and online transfers from a bank account belonging to Energy Eco Bhd.
The funds were allegedly transferred to her personal bank account and an account belonging to Aura Emas Trading Sdn Bhd, a company of which she is a director.
The offences were allegedly committed at three bank branches in Taman Setiawangsa, Wangsa Melawati and Bangsar here between Feb 1, 2021 and Feb 2, 2024.
All the charges were brought under Section 4(1)(b) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (Act 613), which is punishable under Section 4(1) of the same law.
The section provides a maximum prison sentence of 15 years and a fine of not less than five times the amount or value of the proceeds from the unlawful activities, or RM5 million, whichever is higher upon conviction.
Earlier, Deputy Public Prosecutor Nurul Qistini Qamarul Abrar requested that the court apply the existing RM100,000 bail and the additional conditions set in the accused’s previous criminal breach of trust case.
“The prosecution also applies for this case to be tried jointly with the previous case (criminal breach of trust) in this court,” she said.
Lawyer Datuk Gobinath Mohanna, representing Norliza, did not object to the prosecution’s application.
Suzana Hussin subsequently granted the prosecution’s application on bail and for the two cases to be tried jointly. She also set Oct 29 for mention.
On May 11, Norliza and the former Chairman of the Syariah Advisory Council (SAC) of Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM), Tan Sri Dr Mohd Daud Bakar, pleaded not guilty in the same court to seven charges of criminal breach of trust involving RM10.55 million.
In the proceedings, the court granted bail of RM100,000 in one surety each to Norliza and Mohd Daud. They are also ordered to surrender their passports to the court, prohibited from interfering with prosecution witnesses, and to report to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) office once a month. — Bernama

Title: Nilai private university CFO accused of RM6.56m CBT linked to IRB duty payments
Article:
SEREMBAN, Aug 19 — A chief financial officer (CFO) of a private university in Nilai pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to allegedly committing criminal breach of trust involving RM6.56 million in company funds between September 2025 and April this year.
Noraini Aripin, 55, entered the plea after the charge was read out to her before Judge Datin M. Kunasundary Marimuthu.
The charge alleges that Noraini, who was entrusted with RM6,557,720, misused the funds by making payments for purposes other than the payment of ad valorem duty to the Inland Revenue Board (LHDN).
The offence is alleged to have taken place at the university’s office between September 2025 and April this year.
She was charged under Section 409 of the Penal Code (Act 574), which carries a maximum sentence of 20 years’ imprisonment, whipping, and a fine upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Syairah Aqilah Khalil sought bail of RM100,000 with two sureties, with the accused also required to surrender her passport to the court and report to the Negeri Sembilan Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) office each month.
However, lawyer Kelvin Ong requested that bail be reduced to RM50,000, citing his client’s status as a mother of five, her ongoing treatment for stage-three breast cancer at a private hospital and her monthly income of RM15,000.
Bail was later set at RM80,000 with two sureties, with the judge also granting all the prosecution’s requests.
The court set September 21 for the next mention of the case. — Bernama

Title: Former UBB Investment Bank CEO pleads not guilty to RM139.8m cheating charge
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — A former chief executive officer (CEO) of an investment bank pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to a charge of cheating regarding a payment of RM139.8 million to a private university management company.
Razlan Raghazli, 43, the former CEO of UBB Investment Bank Limited, entered the plea after the charge was read out to him before Judge Azura Alwi.
He was charged with cheating the Managing Director and CEO of UBB Amanah Berhad, Aida Aizura Othman, 52, by deceiving her into believing that the payment schedule contained in a UBB Investment Bank Limited letter was in accordance with legal advice.
The letter, titled ‘Disbursement Advice on Islamic Property Financing Under Bai-Bithaman Ajil (BBA)’ dated September 18, 2025, was signed by the accused and stated that it followed legal advice from the firm Kassim Tadin, Wai & Co.
However, the accused allegedly knew that the payment schedule in question actually contradicted the advice provided by the law firm.
The act allegedly caused Aida Aizura to release a payment amounting to RM139,891,776 to ELMU Higher Education Sdn Bhd, a payment she would not have made had she not been deceived in such a manner.
The offence, under Section 420 of the Penal Code, was allegedly committed at the bank in Desa Sri Hartamas in September 2025.
He faces imprisonment of up to 10 years, whipping, and is liable to a fine upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Hazel Tan Jia Qi proposed bail of RM100,000 with one surety, along with additional conditions requiring the accused to surrender his passport to the court and prohibiting him from interfering with or communicating with prosecution witnesses in the case.
However, lawyer Azamuddin Abdul Aziz, representing Razlan, requested that the bail amount be reduced to RM50,000, citing that his client had been unemployed since last June and had to support four children as well as an ailing mother.
Azura then set bail at RM60,000 with the additional conditions requested by the prosecution. She also set October 12 for mention and the submission of documents.
Meanwhile, the proceedings drew attention when lawyer Johan Mohan Abdullah, who is holding a watching brief for UBB, requested a court order prohibiting the media from naming the financial institution in their reports.
He argued that reports naming the institution could potentially undermine financial stability and trigger panic among depositors. However, Azura maintained that the public has a right to know further details regarding the case. — Bernama

Title: Police: Chinese national detained after allegedly disrupting passengers at KLIA, later admitted to psychiatric ward
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 19 — A 27-year-old Chinese national who allegedly behaved aggressively towards passengers at Kuala Lumpur International Airport’s Terminal 1 building is believed to be mentally unwell and has been detained for further investigation, police said today.
KLIA police chief Assistant Commissioner M Ravi said authorities were alerted to the incident involving the woman at about 1.19pm on August 18, after she allegedly began shouting and disturbing passengers in the terminal's departure hall by running, singing and dancing.
"Security personnel later arrived at the scene and managed to calm the situation before bringing the woman to the Terminal 1 police station for further action.
"Her partner later told police that she had forgotten to take her prescribed medication," he said.
The woman was later taken to Hospital Kajang, where she was admitted to the psychiatric ward for further treatment.
He said the woman was scheduled to take a return flight to China that same day, having arrived in Malaysia with her partner as tourists on August 6.
Ravi said the woman was in stable condition and receiving treatment, while embassy officials had been informed of the incident.

Title: Kelana Jaya LRT services back to normal after Putra Heights safety system fault
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Rapid KL said the Kelana Jaya LRT Line resumed normal operations at 9.19am today after inspection and recovery works at Putra Heights station were completed.
The public transport operator said the earlier disruption was caused by a fault involving the station’s safety detection system.
“Checks and recovery measures have been carried out to ensure the system is operating safely,” it said.
Rapid KL said its technical team would continue monitoring the system and train movements to ensure services along the Kelana Jaya Line run smoothly.
It added that all trains have returned to their usual schedules and services affected by the disruption have fully recovered.
Earlier, Rapid KL said services were experiencing delays due to a suspected fault involving a power supply component at Putra Heights station, with trains there operated manually as a safety precaution.
Rapid KL apologised to passengers for the inconvenience caused by the train delays.

Title: Delays on Kelana Jaya LRT Line after suspected power supply fault
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Rapid KL said today that services on the Kelana Jaya LRT Line are experiencing delays due to a suspected fault involving a power supply component at Putra Heights station.
In a statement posted on Facebook, the public transport operator said trains at Putra Heights are being operated manually as a safety precaution.
It said this would also slow train movements at nearby stations and result in longer waiting times for passengers on platforms.
Rapid KL said its technical team has been deployed to the station to carry out checks and restore normal operations as soon as possible.
Auxiliary police and station personnel have also been stationed at concourse and platform areas to assist passengers, while regular announcements on train schedules are being made at stations.
Passengers were advised to check Rapid KL’s social media channels or the MyRapid PULSE journey-planning app for the latest updates on Kelana Jaya Line services.

Title: Saifuddin Nasution hits out at recycled false claims of Home Ministry granting citizenship en masse to foreigners
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 19 — Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail has denied claims that the Home Ministry (KDN) granted citizenship en masse to foreign nationals and that 1.2 million Chinese nationals had remained in Malaysia.
Saifuddin Nasution said he had denied the allegations on numerous occasions, but some people continued to deliberately recycle videos, posters and narratives relating to the issue.
“I have repeatedly rejected these claims and have provided explanations backed by facts and official data.
“Yet some parties continue to deliberately recycle videos, posters and narratives that have already been corrected to confuse the public and stir racial tensions and hatred,” he said in a post on his official social media accounts today.
Saifuddin Nasution said the matter had already been explained officially, with the facts documented in earlier statements and media reports.
“The dissemination of such defamatory claims not only tarnishes the reputation of individuals or institutions, but more worryingly, can undermine public confidence in state institutions, stir racial hatred, disrupt public order and threaten national security,” he said.
He urged everyone to stop spreading such claims and not to exploit sensitive issues for political interests or social media attention.
“I also call on the public to check the accuracy of information with official sources before accepting or sharing it.
“Use social media responsibly. Facts are facts, and data is data. Do not let false claims override the truth,” he said.
Several posters alleging that KDN had granted citizenship to foreigners en masse have been widely circulated on social media. — Bernama
